findings.summary: The orchestration lane pins the resolve child receipt, but each bounded node replaces link.subagentRunId, so later lifecycle events are rejected as stale.
evidence: The orchestration lane stores the receipt returned by startIssue in lane.started, while #dispatchNode assigns link.subagentRunId = receipt.runId for every non-reviewer node at work-on.ts:1840; reviewer launches leave a launch sentinel because the assignment is inside the !reviewerNode branch.
The ready/completed parent path emits link.subagentRunId at work-on.ts:1565, which is therefore a later node receipt (or reviewer sentinel), not the receipt stored in the lane.

orchestrate.ts:355 returns whenever event.subagentRunId differs from lane.subagentRunId. After prepare-pr/review this differs deterministically, so lane.ready, lane.failed, and lane.completed events are ignored and orchestration cannot integrate or finish the issue.

findings.summary: Fresh bounded implementation nodes receive only a generic handoff instead of the issue and plan, so they cannot reliably implement the requested behavior.
evidence: startIssue builds the issue title/body/labels JSON once for resolve, but after every node #reconcileNode dispatches the next node with the literal 'Resume from durable node artifacts only.' at work-on.ts:1066.
SubagentsRpcClient forwards that value as the bounded task's issueContext at subagents.ts:266; no issue or plan artifact is included in the ActiveRunLink or launch input.

The bounded task forbids bash for implement at subagents.ts:263, child-runtime blocks bash outside resolve/investigate/plan at child-runtime.ts:171-179, and allowedNodeTools('implement') exposes only forge_diff/forge_commit/forge_finalize_node at child-runtime.ts:1054. The fresh implement worker has no issue/GitHub/state access; remediation additionally only says to read inaccessible durable artifacts at work-on.ts:1787-1788.

findings.summary: Controller restart cannot reconcile a parent-owned node because attach only resumes active child receipts and never dispatches currentNodeId parent work.
evidence: #dispatchNode routes review-join, ci, decision, merge, close, and cleanup directly into #runParentNode while persisting currentNodeId, with no activeNodes entry (work-on.ts:1662-1666).

On attach, the recovery loop at work-on.ts:238-266 handles only activeNodes; when that map is empty it checks a launch sentinel or calls rpc.status and waits for a legacy ForgeWorkOnResult (work-on.ts:267-279). It never checks parentNodeFromId/currentNodeId or calls #runParentNode.

A crash during a parent operation therefore leaves its durable node running and the restored link unable to progress; for a standalone run the lease also remains held despite no resumable provider child.

findings.summary: Integration selects the first completed decision rather than the latest awaiting-merge decision, so a successful remediation round cannot merge.
evidence: The decision node deliberately records outcome remediation-required when fixable findings remain and another review round is allowed (work-on.ts:1422-1424), after which dispatcher creates a later decision node.

integrateIssue uses Object.values(current.state.nodes).find(...) at work-on.ts:2080. Object insertion order places decision-1 before decision-2, so after round two is approved it selects the old remediation-required decision.
The next line rejects that result unless outcome is awaiting-merge, causing orchestration integration to throw and the lane to be marked failed even though the latest review passed.

findings.summary: Short reviewer aliases accepted by the finalizer are not normalized before the review gate, causing a false incomplete-panel block.
evidence: forge_finalize_reviewer explicitly accepts either 'security' or 'forge-review-security' (and the correctness equivalents) at child-runtime.ts:689-696; #loadReviewerResult accepts the same aliases at work-on.ts:1088-1095.
#aggregateFromState copies reviewer.reviewer verbatim into completedReviewers at work-on.ts:1649.

The configured policy requires full names ('forge-review-correctness' and 'forge-review-security'), and evaluateReviewGate compares completedReviewers literally. A valid result using reviewer:'security' is consequently treated as a missing required reviewer and cannot merge.

findings.summary: The bounded parent dispatcher never advances workflow labels after starting/reviewing, leaving completed or invalid issues misclassified.
evidence: The new start path sets only workflow:investigating at work-on.ts:596; bounded artifact reconciliation posts comments at work-on.ts:867 without setting a workflow label.

forge_prepare_review sets workflow:in-review in child-runtime.ts:647, but the parent decision/merge/close/cleanup path at work-on.ts:1560-1584 only posts artifacts and node events; it never sets workflow:awaiting-merge, workflow:merged, workflow:invalid, or workflow:decomposed.
The only workflow:merged call is in the legacy #finalize path at work-on.ts:2732-2735, which the bounded node dispatcher does not invoke, so normal bounded runs leave GitHub issue labels stale.

limitations: Tests and typecheck were not executed in this read-only review; findings are based on static inspection of the frozen worktree and its tests.

findings.summary: Read-only nodes can execute unrestricted bash with the parent environment.
evidence: The tool_call hook returns immediately for bash on resolve, investigate, and plan nodes; it does not inspect or allowlist the command (lines 171-181).
FORGE_WORK_ON_TOOLS exposes bash to every bounded writer node (src/agents/register.ts:20-24), so the hook is the only command boundary.

The native bash path is not run through safeEnvironment; a prompt-injected issue can invoke gh/git/curl, read user files or GitHub CLI credentials, and perform GitHub writes or pushes despite the read-only node contract.

findings.summary: The child guard does not make resolve/investigate/plan read-only: write and edit are permitted on any in-worktree path.
evidence: After the Forge-tool check, the hook handles read/write/edit/grep/find/ls only by checking path containment and then returns; there is no node-based denial for write or edit (lines 187-204).
The same FORGE_WORK_ON_TOOLS list gives write and edit to every bounded node (src/agents/register.ts:20-29).

A resolve or investigate child can therefore modify source, workflow, or policy files before implementation; later forge_commit stages every changed path via git add -A -- ...changedPaths (child-runtime.ts:410-422), with no accepted-plan allowlist or clean-boundary check.

findings.summary: Agent materialization follows repository-controlled symlinks and can overwrite files outside the Forge runtime directory.
evidence: materializeForgeAgents is called on the freshly checked-out worktree before the child starts (src/workflows/work-on.ts:555).

The implementation creates .pi/agents with mkdir but never rejects symlink components, then writes fixed agent filenames with writeFile; writeFile follows a tracked symlink at .pi/agents/forge-work-on.md (materialize.ts:25-27, 97-101).

A repository can commit that path as a symlink to another tracked file, an external writable path, or a host configuration file; the write occurs as the user and can corrupt source/policy data or overwrite an outside file before any child path guard runs.

findings.summary: The model-callable forge_orchestrate tool has no enforced user confirmation and always authorizes expired-lease takeover.
evidence: The tool description asks the LLM to resolve and confirm, but execute ignores sourceExpression and resolutionSummary and unconditionally calls orchestrator.start with allowExpiredTakeover: true (commands.ts:27-50).

orchestrate.start uses that boolean to cancel the expired orchestration and release its lease without an authorization identity (workflows/orchestrate.ts:158-174); the only confirmation requirement is prompt text.

An indirect prompt injection in GitHub issue text, or any direct model tool call, can dispatch arbitrary positive issue numbers and cancel a prior orchestration; with auto-merge policy this can launch writes/merges without the promised operator approval.
